verdict.thesis: Fundamentals are intact; the BUY's edge isn't. The filed Q2 inflection (+50% revenue, 53.8% gross margin) and the Helios story are consensus-owned, 19.3x sales leaves no margin of safety, and the leadership leg that justified buying early lagged SPY 4.6 pts [P1]. Our post-print 'filed inflection' BUYs are 0-for-3 [P1][P3][P5]: a reported quarter isn't a catalyst. Upside must come from beating $13.92 forward EPS, not re-rating [K1]; that test is dated 11/3. Keep the starter and 200-day kill line as a documented no-add HOLD [K3].
verdict.bear_risk: On 11/3 Helios ramps at sub-50% gross margin with opex stepping up again and a Data Center guide below the 70-80% framing, exposing the $13.92 forward EPS against a $3.01 TTM base and de-rating a 19.3x-sales, maximally-long-consensus name in a single session.
verdict.watch_trigger: Re-rate to BUY and build toward full weight after the print if 11/3 holds gross margin at or above 50% through the first Helios revenue quarter with a Data Center guide at 70-80%+; exit the starter on a decisive weekly close below the 200-day or a sub-50% gross-margin print.
verdict.memory_note: Memory weakened the view: the 8/5 BUY itself lagged SPY 4.6 pts [P1] and the post-print 'filed inflection' template is 0-for-3 [P1][P3][P5], stripping the leadership leg and the BUY label, but overlapping, semis-heavy windows (effective n near 3) make it a conviction trim from 58 to 52, not grounds to exit without a fundamental break.
